topics.title: Responsive layout
topics.summary: Sizes, rows and columns, stacks, scrolling and screen sizes beyond the base: every layout field, which sizing modes each parent allows, media rules and breakpoints, and the web layouts agents ask for (a capped band, cards that wrap, a row that becomes a column, overlap and bleed, a sticky header or column).

topics.title: Layout fields
topics.summary: A node's `"layout"`: its size, spacing and placement in its parent.

topics.title: Which sizing modes each parent allows
topics.summary: From the parents' own rules; "fill (with `basis`)": a child of a wrapping row may fill its line's share when it sets `layout.basis`.

topics.title: Media rules
topics.summary: A node's `media` (and the theme's) is a list of rules, each a CSS media query over the node:

topics.title: Breakpoints
topics.summary: The project's breakpoints name size classes by minimum width.

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: Responsive design
topics.summary: Responsive layout works as on the web: flexbox and grid lay content out so it fits any width, and media queries change what must change at a width.

topics.title: A capped band
topics.summary: A full-width band with capped, centered content (CSS `max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto` inside a coloured band): the band fills the width and holds the background; its one child fills with `constraints.maxWidth`, centered by the band's `crossAxisAlignment` (`center`, the default).

topics.title: An editorial page at three sizes
topics.summary: A phone, a tablet and a desktop are three layouts, not one stretched: **use the width**.

topics.title: Grid spans; a timetable
topics.summary: A `gridView` item spans and is placed as in CSS grid, through its own `layout` (the template's, bound per item from its data, and patched per size like any field):

topics.title: Cards that wrap
topics.summary: Three plan cards three across at desktop, two at tablet, one on phones, with no breakpoint: a wrapping `row` (`"wrap": true`, `spacing`, `runSpacing`) whose cards are `"width": {"fill": 300}, "basis": 280`.

topics.title: A row that becomes a column
topics.summary: A `flex` node with `"direction": "horizontal"` and a rule patching `"direction": "vertical"` below a width.

topics.title: A media rule and a binding on one field
topics.summary: Shown on phones only, and there only while a panel is closed: a patch may set `bind`, bindings that hold at its sizes only.

topics.title: Overlap and bleed
topics.summary: **Overlapping a neighbour** (CSS `margin-top: -36px`, `transform: translateY(-36px)`): Flutter's answer is `Transform.translate`: `"motion": {"translateY": -36}` moves what the node paints, not its layout, so the next node does not move up; a node later in its parent paints over the ones before it.

topics.title: Scrolling
topics.summary: A screen scrolls only if something in it scrolls.

topics.title: A sticky header or column
topics.summary: A header that stays at the top while the page scrolls under it: the scrolling column's first child with `"sticky": {"offset": 0}` (CSS `position: sticky`); it is drawn above the content and is pushed on by the end of its parent.

topics.title: A canvas per breakpoint
topics.summary: Canvases with the same `props.screen` are one screen; each sets `props.breakpoint` to the breakpoint it is for.

topics.title: Theme and text
topics.summary: A site's palette and type scale, declared once and named everywhere; dark mode and a type scale that changes with the screen size; and the `text` node in depth (runs, links, superscripts, fonts, text direction).

topics.title: Theme keys
topics.summary: The theme (`site.json`'s `theme`, or the app's theme at run time):

topics.title: Named colours and styles
topics.summary: - **Colours**: `colors` maps a name to `"#AARRGGBB"` (or to another colour's name: `"accent": "ember"`).

topics.title: What controls take from the theme
topics.summary: A control's colours, fonts and shapes that its props leave unset come from the theme: `primary` fills filled buttons (labelled in `onPrimary`) and draws checks, thumbs, focus rings and text-button labels where it reads on `surface` (else `onSurface` does); `fontFamily` is every control label's font (`titleFontFamily` titles'); `buttonRadius` shapes every kind of button and chip, `radius` dialogs, menus and pickers.

topics.title: A type scale that changes with the screen size
topics.summary: The theme's `media` rules patch the theme as a node's rules patch a node: `{"minWidth": 1024, "patch": {"textStyles": {"title": {"fontSize": 56}}}}` makes every text using `title` grow at desktop width, written once.

topics.title: Dark mode
topics.summary: `"dark": {"colors": {"ink": "#FFEEEEEE"}}` gives the colours that differ in dark mode; a node naming `ink` follows the device's mode.

topics.title: Text
topics.summary: A `text` node has `props.text` and `props.style`.

topics.title: Superscripts and a raised currency sign
topics.summary: A raised or lowered character (a price's "$", a footnote mark): a run with `"fontFeatures": ["sups"]` (or `"subs"`) when the font has those OpenType features; otherwise a smaller `fontSize` in a row of texts aligned `crossAxisAlignment: start` (or `baseline`) for the exact shift.

topics.title: Fonts
topics.summary: `style.fontFamily` names a family (`"Inter"`), with `fontWeight` choosing the file.

topics.title: Decoration, images, icons and drawing
topics.summary: What a node's box paints beyond the base: gradients, pixel patterns and grain, borders on some sides, shadows and blurs, scrims over children, images, icons, SVG-like paths and custom drawing.

topics.title: Decoration fields
topics.summary: A node's `"decoration"`: what its box paints.

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: Gradients
topics.summary: As Flutter's `LinearGradient`, a linear gradient runs from `"begin"` to `"end"` (alignments; default left to right; `[0, -1]` to `[0, 1]` is top to bottom).

topics.title: A pattern in pixels, a background grid, grain
topics.summary: **A pattern in pixels** (CSS `repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, #E5E7EB 0 1px, transparent 1px 80px)`): a linear gradient with `"length": 80` (px from `begin` toward `end`) and `"tileMode": "repeated"`; a background grid is two of them, one `topCenter` → `bottomCenter`, one `centerLeft` → `centerRight`.

topics.title: Borders, rules and shadows
topics.summary: A node's border is painted with its own box, **under its children**: a child with a fill covers an `inside` border (the default).

topics.title: A scrim over a photo
topics.summary: `foregroundFills` paint over the node **and its children**, as Flutter's `foregroundDecoration`: a scrim there darkens a caption inside the node too.

topics.title: Images
topics.summary: Images are image fills: `{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "...", "fit": "cover"}}` in `decoration.fills` of a box (give the box the image's size or an `aspectRatio`).

topics.title: Icons
topics.summary: An `icon` node with `props.icon` set to a Material icon name (`"check_circle"`, `"menu"`, `"north_east"`; any name at fonts.google.com/icons; `_outlined`, `_rounded`, `_sharp` pick the style), `props.color` and `props.size` (the glyph's size, centered in the node's box; without it the glyph fills the box).

topics.title: Small marks and shapes
topics.summary: A mark the font lacks (✦, ✳): an `icon` (`"auto_awesome"`, `"star"`), or a `path` node with SVG path data and a `viewBox` so it scales to its box: the one decorated shape (fills, strokes and shadows from its `decoration`).

topics.title: Buttons, forms and inputs
topics.summary: Buttons, text fields, checkboxes, switches, radios, sliders, dropdowns, segmented buttons, date and time pickers, chips and signatures: every control's props, **how to style each one (in one place, below)**, two-way binding to a variable, validation and error states, focus and the keyboard.

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: Styling the controls, in one place
topics.summary: Every colour there may be a theme colour's name; every text style may name a theme style.

topics.title: A text field bound to a variable (two-way)
topics.summary: Bind its `props.initialValue` to the variable: `"bind": {"props.initialValue": "${query}"}`.

topics.title: Validation and an error state
topics.summary: As Flutter's `TextFormField` and `Form`:

topics.title: A radio group
topics.summary: Flutter's `RadioGroup`: give the node around the radios `"radioGroup": {"groupValue": ...}`, bind its `radioGroup.groupValue` to the variable that keeps the choice, and store `${result}` in its `changed` reaction.

topics.title: A stepper around a field
topics.summary: Two icon buttons that `setVariable` with `"op": "add"` / `"subtract"` on a number, and a field bound two-way to the same variable.

topics.title: A clear button in the field
topics.summary: Its `decoration.suffixIcon` with a tap reaction (`actions` is a list of reactions, as a node's), shown only while there is text by binding the icon:

topics.title: A labelled checkbox or switch
topics.summary: The whole row toggles: the control ignores the pointer and shows the variable; the row's reaction toggles it.

topics.title: Buttons
topics.summary: Buttons (`filledButton`, `elevatedButton`, `outlinedButton`, `textButton`, `iconButton`) take `label` and `style`.

topics.title: Add and remove items (a list editor)
topics.summary: Add: `setVariable` on the list with `"op": "add"` (appends; a list value appends each item) and `"value": "${= object('name', draft, 'done', false)}"`, then clear the draft; guard it with the action's `when` (or an `if`) on the draft not being empty.

topics.title: Focus and the keyboard
topics.summary: `focus` moves the focus to a field (or away), `editText` changes its text or selection.

topics.title: Lists, grids, tables and repeated data
topics.summary: Anything repeated from data: lists and grids from one item template, nested lists (`item`, `index`, `parent`), equal-height card grids, tables, carousels (`pageView`), list tiles, pagination, pull to refresh, swipe actions and reordering.

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: One template from data
topics.summary: A `listView` (or `gridView`, `pageView`) repeats its **first child** once per item of its `data` binding: `"bind": {"data": "${questions}"}`.

topics.title: A grid of cards
topics.summary: For cards in columns from one list inside a scrolling page, use a `gridView` with `minCrossAxisExtent` (CSS `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))`: as many equal columns as fit), `"shrinkWrapRows": true` and `"physics": "never"` (it lays out every item and the page scrolls).

topics.title: Equal-height cards
topics.summary: In a `gridView` with `"shrinkWrapRows": true` (CSS grid's auto rows) each row is as tall as its tallest item, and every item is stretched to it, whether it hugs or fills its height.

topics.title: Nested lists
topics.summary: A list inside a list's item repeats per item of its own `data`, usually a field of the outer item.

topics.title: A table from one template
topics.summary: A `listView` of rows bound to the records, each row a label and a `gridView` of cells bound to `${item.values}` with `crossAxisCount` the number of columns: one cell node for every column (the example in $1).

topics.title: A weekly grid
topics.summary: Seven columns of days from data: a `gridView` with `"crossAxisCount": 7` bound to the days (`${= range(7)}`, or a computed list of `{day, done}` records), each cell a box whose fill is bound to the item.

topics.title: A carousel, pages and pagination
topics.summary: A `pageView` shows one item (or child) per page and swipes between them (`viewportFraction` below 1 shows the neighbours' edges; `initialPage`).

topics.title: Screens, navigation, modals and toasts
topics.summary: Several screens and moving between them, a page's URL path, passing values to a screen, dialogs, bottom sheets and popovers, confirmations and toasts, app bars, navigation bars, tabs and disclosure (accordions).

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: Screens
topics.summary: Each canvas in `roots` is a screen, unless canvases are grouped: canvases with the same `props.screen` are one screen, one canvas per breakpoint ($1).

topics.title: Going to a screen and back
topics.summary: `{"type": "navigate", "to": "<canvas id>"}` pushes the screen; `"mode": "pop"` goes back; `"replace"` and `"reset"` replace the history.

topics.title: Modals and toasts
topics.summary: `{"type": "openModal", "to": "<canvas id>"}` shows another canvas over the screen, at its design size (`presentation`: `dialog`, `bottomSheet`, `fullScreen`, a popover anchored to a node...).

topics.title: A mobile menu (drawer)
topics.summary: A menu button that toggles a `menuOpen` variable, and the menu a node bound `"visible": "${menuOpen}"`.

topics.title: Tabs and an accordion (FAQ)
topics.summary: Tabs from a variable: a row of tab labels whose `selected` binds to `${= tab == 'lunch'}` with a click that sets `tab`, and the panels bound `visible` on `tab` (the `tabs` and `tabBar` node types do the same with Material's look).

topics.title: App bars and navigation bars
topics.summary: A canvas's `appBar` slot spans the top at its own height and `bottomNavigationBar` the bottom; the body sits between, and `floatingActionButton` sits 16 px from the right above the bottom bar.

topics.title: State and logic
topics.summary: Variables and where they live, computed and function variables, expressions and every binding path with the value it expects, conditions, the formula functions (grouped: text, numbers, money, lists, objects, dates, colours), the actions that change state, and sandboxed scripts.

topics.title: Variables
topics.summary: Declare them in the document's `variables`, under a canvas id (that canvas only) or under `"page_variables"` (every canvas of the document, kept while the user moves between them).

topics.title: Expressions
topics.summary: `${name}` or `${path}` reads a value: `${count}`, `${user.name}`, `${items[0].price}`, `${pal[item.kind]}`.

topics.title: Binding paths
topics.summary: What each path of `bind` expects.

topics.title: Conditions
topics.summary: An if / else-if / else rule.

topics.title: Scripts
topics.summary: A document's sandboxed JavaScript (`scripts`), run by `runScript` or called from a formula (`script.name(...)`).

topics.title: Formula functions
topics.summary: The functions a formula (`${= ...}`) can call, from the SDK's formula engine, grouped.

topics.title: Text
topics.summary: (Continues: state.md#state-text.)

topics.title: Lists
topics.summary: (Continues: state.md#state-lists.)

topics.title: Dates and time
topics.summary: (Continues: state.md#state-dates-and-time.)

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: Computed and function variables
topics.summary: A variable with a `formula` (what goes in `${= ...}`) is read-only and follows what it reads; with `parameters` it is a function any formula calls by name.

topics.title: A streak and other counts from data
topics.summary: Derive, do not store: a computed variable over the records.

topics.title: Changing state from a reaction
topics.summary: `setVariable` with `op`: `set` (default), `toggle`, `add` (a number adds; a list appends; a map merges), `subtract`, `insert` / `removeAt` / `update` at `index`, `remove`.

topics.title: Setting several nodes with a condition
topics.summary: A condition sets node fields while a test holds: an ordered list of branches (if, else if, ..., else) under a canvas id in the document's `conditions`.

topics.title: When to use a script
topics.summary: For multi-step state changes (a puzzle's checks, a game step, a streak over dates), a script reads and sets variables with `vars.get(name)` and `vars.set(name, value)` (capabilities `variables.read`, `variables.write`); the UI updates through what binds to them.

topics.title: Interaction: reactions, states and gestures
topics.summary: What a node does when it is tapped, hovered, pressed, dragged or swiped: reactions and every trigger, hover and pressed styles (`states`), ink ripples, tooltips, letting taps through, drag and drop, values set by dragging (`track`), swipe to dismiss, pan, pinch and rotate, keys, the clipboard and haptics.

topics.title: Trigger fields
topics.summary: A trigger is `{"type": "<type>", ...these}`, or just the type as a string (`"click"`).

topics.title: Fields every action has
topics.summary: Fields holding nested action chains (a list of actions): `then`, `else`, `actions`, `onSuccess`, `onError`, `cancelActions`.

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: Reactions
topics.summary: A node's `actions` is a list of **reactions**: a trigger and the chain of actions it runs, in order.

topics.title: Hover, press and other states
topics.summary: `states` on a node changes it and its descendants while it is `hovered`, `pressed`, `focused`, `selected`, `disabled` or `dragged`.

topics.title: A segmented toggle (monthly / annual)
topics.summary: Two labels in a row with a fill; each label's `selected` binds to the variable (`${= annual}` and `${= !annual}`), its `states.selected` patches its fill and text colour, and its click sets the variable.

topics.title: Drag and drop
topics.summary: `draggable` (`{"group": "card", "data": "${item.id}"}`) lets the node be picked up; a `dropTarget` that `accepts` the group takes it, and its `drop` reaction reads the data as `${result}`.

topics.title: Values set by dragging, swiping, pinching
topics.summary: `track` sets a variable as the pointer moves along a line, arc or path (a custom slider, a dial).

topics.title: Keys
topics.summary: A canvas's `keyDown` reaction (`{"trigger": {"type": "keyDown", "key": "ArrowRight"}, ...}`) runs while no text field has the focus: arrow keys between tabs are two reactions that set the tab variable (`${= (tabIndex + 1) % 4}`), Escape closing a menu is one.

topics.title: Animation and motion
topics.summary: Anything that moves: a change that animates (implicit transitions), keyframe animations and presets, moving, scaling and turning a node without changing layout (`motion`), shared-element flights (`hero`), reveal on scroll, shimmer, typewriter text, particles, flip cards and tilt, and the timer and frame triggers for clocks and games.

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: Animate a change (transitions)
topics.summary: `transitions` is Flutter's implicit animation: when the value at a path changes (a binding, a condition, a state patch), the node tweens from what it shows to the new value.

topics.title: Move, scale or turn without changing layout (motion)
topics.summary: `motion` is a transform painted over the node's layout (Flutter's `Transform`): `translateX`/`translateY` in pixels, `scale`, `rotate` in degrees, 3D `rotateX`/`rotateY` with `perspective`, about `alignment` (the center by default).

topics.title: Play an animation (animations and presets)
topics.summary: `animations` holds a node's controllers: each runs 0 → 1 over `duration` (or a `spring`), after `delay`, once or `repeat`ed, and drives `tracks` of keyframes on its paths.

topics.title: Reveal on scroll, view progress, sticky effects
topics.summary: `reveal` plays when the node scrolls into view; `viewProgress` gives `${view.progress}` (0–1 through the viewport) to bind to; the `enterViewport` and `exitViewport` triggers run actions.

topics.title: Shared elements (hero)
topics.summary: `hero` is Flutter's `Hero`: a tag (`"hero": "avatar-${item.id}"`) flies the node from its place on the screen a navigation leaves to the node with the same tag on the screen it opens; `flightShuttle` picks what flies (`morph`, `containerTransform`...).

topics.title: Clocks and game loops
topics.summary: A canvas's `timer` trigger (`"intervalMs": 1000`, `"when"`: a formula that must hold) runs every interval (`${result.tick}` counts); `frame` runs every frame while `when` holds (`${result.dt}` ms since the last), for physics and game loops.

topics.title: Components and sections
topics.summary: Splitting a page into parts, each a file: a component used in several places with different values (a card, a chip, a row), a section used once (a header, a hero, an FAQ), their parameters (every kind, `variable` included), slots and events, the site manifest, and when to use a component, a list template or a section.

topics.title: Parameter kinds
topics.summary: Declared in `widget.props` as the catalog declares any prop: `key`, `type` (`kind` and the Flutter type; `min`, `max`, enum `values`, list `item`), `default`, `doc`, and `"required": true` for one a call must set.

topics.title: The site manifest
topics.summary: A directory with a `site.json` is a site: its pages, its components and its project variables, read by bare name in every page and component (a page or component variable of the same name is `duplicate_variable`).

topics.title: Validation codes
topics.summary: `unknown_component` (a call to a type no definition declares), `duplicate_component`, `component_cycle` (a component calling itself, directly or through others), `component_id_mismatch` (the file is not named after its type), `invalid_component`, `missing_prop`, `unknown_event`, `call_field_not_allowed`, `slot_outside_component`, `root_placement_bound`.

topics.title: Triggers
topics.summary: Written as `"trigger": {"type": "<trigger>", ...}` in a reaction ($1).

topics.title: Components are Flutter widget classes
topics.summary: A page can be split into parts, each in a file of its own: a **component** is a document with one root (not a canvas) and a `widget` declaration, and a page (or another component) **calls** it with one node whose `type` is the component's type.

topics.title: When to make what
topics.summary: * **List template**: one shape repeated from data in one parent.

topics.title: What a definition reads
topics.summary: Its parameters (`props`), its own variables (one set per instance: two chips are hovered apart), the project's variables (`site.json`, below) and the runtime's scopes (`screen`, `route`, `theme`, `auth`...); inside its own lists, `item` and `index`.

topics.title: Computed values inside a definition
topics.summary: A definition's own variables may be computed from its parameters: `{"name": "over", "type": "boolean", "formula": "props.seats > props.limit"}` under the root's id in its `variables`, then `${over}` in any of its nodes.

topics.title: Shared state: variable parameters
topics.summary: share state with the caller: `{"kind": "variable", "of": {"kind": "boolean"}}`.

topics.title: Slots
topics.summary: A `slot` node in the definition is replaced by what the call passes: the call's `children` for the slot named `children` (the default name; declare `"children": "list"`), or the call's `slots[name]` for a named slot (declare it in `widget.slots`).

topics.title: Events
topics.summary: Declared in `widget.events`; fired inside with `{"type": "componentEvent", "event": "onRemove", "value": ...}`; handled by the call's reaction `{"trigger": {"type": "event", "event": "onRemove"}}`, which runs in the caller's scope with the value as `${result}`.

topics.title: Size and place
topics.summary: The call and the definition's root are one box: the call's `layout` sizes and places it (width, height, flex, margin, x/y, align, constraints); the root keeps its padding, decoration and contents.

topics.title: Ids and paths
topics.summary: A definition's ids are its own (`text`, `remove`); a page may use the same ids, and diagnostics name a node of an instance by its path, so the two never mix.

topics.title: Rendering one part
topics.summary: `tool/render/render.sh site --out out --component Chip` renders the component alone, once per preview at its size; `--props '{"label": "Long label"}'` renders one parameter set at each size, and `--slots fixture.json` (`{"children": [ids], "slots": {"leading": id}, "nodes": {...}}`) passes slot content.

topics.title: Per instance
topics.summary: Everything a definition keeps is kept per instance, as a Flutter `State` is: its variables, its interaction states, the values a `setValue` (or `setVariant`) sets on its nodes (set inside an instance, they change that instance's node only).

topics.title: Published components
topics.summary: A published site carries its components beside its pages (each at `publish/{project}/components/{Type}`, with a version and a digest; a bundle holds them in its `components` map), and an app loads the ones a screen calls with the screen, caches them, and follows a republished one: every instance updates where it is, without reloading the pages that call it.

topics.title: Charts, gauges and indicators
topics.summary: Showing numbers as pictures: progress bars and rings, activity spinners, badges, gauges, bar, line and series charts, scatter plots and barcodes.

topics.title: Progress from state
topics.summary: Bind the value (`"bind": {"props.value": "${done}"}`) with `max` the goal; `"animate": true` eases changes.

topics.title: Charts from data
topics.summary: `barChart` and `lineChart` take plain lists (`values`, `labels`); bind them to computed variables (`${= map(week, d => d.count)}`).

topics.title: Data: APIs, cloud data, storage and form submission
topics.summary: The `data` feature library: calling HTTP APIs, reading and writing the project's cloud documents and files, storing values on the device, and submitting forms.

topics.title: Call an API and show the result
topics.summary: `callApi` names an API of the publish model (`services.apis`: method, URL, headers, body with `${input}` placeholders) and passes `params`; its result is `${result}` in `onSuccess` (store it with `setVariable`), the error in `onError`.

topics.title: Cloud documents
topics.summary: `cloudData` creates, updates, deletes, reads, queries or aggregates documents of a collection (`whereFilters`, `orderByFilters`, `limit`); its result goes in `resultVariable`.

topics.title: Storage on the device
topics.summary: `setStorage` writes `${storage.<key>}` (a key may be a path into a stored map or list; `op` as `setVariable`'s).

topics.title: Submit a form
topics.summary: `submitForm` validates the answers and stores them (`service: local`), or sends them to a destination the project declares; `onSuccess` and `onError` run after.

topics.title: Auth: signing users in
topics.summary: The `auth` feature library: signing app users in, up and out, and managing their account, with `${auth}` to show who is signed in.

topics.title: Show the signed-in user
topics.summary: `${auth.isSignedIn}`, `${auth.email}`, `${auth.displayName}`, `${auth.initial}`, `${auth.role}` bind like any value: a header shows "Sign in" or the user's name by `visible` bindings on `${auth.isSignedIn}`.

topics.title: Errors
topics.summary: A failure's message goes in `errorVariable` and stops the chain: actions after `auth` run only on success.

topics.title: Commerce: paywalls
topics.summary: The `commerce` feature library: a paywall screen's interactions (buy, restore, select a product, close, open a legal link).

topics.title: A paywall screen
topics.summary: The products and offers come from the project's paywall placement; the screen is an ordinary canvas whose buttons run `paywall` operations (`selectProduct`, then `purchase`; `restore`; `closePaywall`; `openLegalLink`).

topics.title: Media: video, audio, web views, speech and sound
topics.summary: The `media` feature library: video players, embedded videos, an audio player, web views, reading text aloud, playing sounds, printing, capturing a screenshot, downloading a file and preloading images.

topics.title: Control a player from state

topics.title: Edit ops and streaming
topics.summary: Building and changing a document with edit operations: what a model sends in a `ui_apply` tool call, what an app's `UiSession` applies while the model streams, the retry protocol for rejected ops, the tools' schemas and the trust profiles that limit what a model may use.

topics.title: The ops
topics.summary: A document is built and changed with six **edit operations**, each addressed by node id: what an agent sends in a `ui_apply` tool call, what `codelessly apply` takes, and what an app's `UiSession` applies while a model streams (`applyOps`, `decodeOps`, `OpStreamDecoder` in `package:codelessly_api/core.dart`).

topics.title: The tools
topics.summary: `outline(document)` is one row per node, `[id, type, label, depth, {what is bound, states, triggers}]`, a sixth to a seventh of the document's size (the two m05 pages: 6.7 KB for 147 nodes against 47.6 KB, 8.3 KB for 196 nodes against 55.4 KB).

topics.title: The trust profile
topics.summary: `TrustProfile` is what an edited document may use: node types and action types (a restricted catalog, `profile.restrict(catalog)`), scripts, link and image hosts, navigation, and limits (nodes, depth, text length, ops per call).

topics.title: Streaming

topics.title: The retry protocol
topics.summary: After a stream, the tool result (`EditResult.toModelJson()`) says exactly what the document holds and what to do: `rev`, the ops that applied (by index, and the ids they set, patched, moved and removed), every rejected op with its code, path, what was expected and a suggestion, warnings (at most 20), the pending ids, the document's roots and node count, and, when anything was rejected or is pending, `next`: fix it by patching the document as it is (same ids), never start over.

topics.title: The render command: checking your work
topics.summary: Checking a document or a site before trusting it: strict validation, screenshots at each size, the states after taps, typing and scrolling, and a diagnostic for every problem with a code, a JSON pointer and what to do.

topics.title: What it does
topics.summary: Decoding is lenient: a misspelled key, a value of the wrong shape or an unknown enum value is silently ignored or replaced by its default.

topics.title: Steps before the capture
topics.summary: In order: `--tap <id>` (`<id>#<n>` for the n-th copy of a list item; a node out of view or under an overlay is scrolled to the middle first, and a tap that would land on another node is reported, not made), `--hover <id>`, `--focus <id>`, `--unfocus`, `--type <id>=<text>`, `--key <key>`, `--set <variable>=<json>`, `--scroll <id or screen>=<px>`, `--navigate <canvas id>`, `--wait <ms>`.
